text.en: From holding a single breath in Kabaddi to dodging in Kho-Kho and mastering leverage on Judo and Wrestling mats, Chapter 7 explores traditional Indian and combative sports.

Chapter 7 covers two indigenous Indian team games—Kabaddi and Kho-Kho—and two combative Olympic sports—Judo and Wrestling.
Kabaddi requires no equipment: a 13×10 m court (men) or 12×8 m (women). A raider holds one breath chanting 'kabaddi, kabaddi' (called 'cant'). Touching antis scores 1 point each; getting all opponents out earns a 2-point bonus called 'Lona'.
Kho-Kho has 12-player squads (9 on field) and two innings of 9-minute chasing and running turns. Sitting chasers face alternate directions and can only run one way, while dodgers may run between them.
Judo ('ju' = gentle, 'do' = way) was developed in Japan using balance and leverage; three officials (1 referee, 2 judges) oversee bouts on a mat with blue and white starting tapes 4 m apart.
Wrestling (ancient Indian 'Malla Yuddha') is contested on a 9 m circular mat by 3 officials (referee, chairperson, judge) in two 3-minute periods (juniors/seniors).
In Greco-Roman wrestling, holds below the waist and using legs to trip are forbidden; in Freestyle, both arms and legs may be used.
Kabaddi and Kho-Kho are fast, low-cost indigenous Indian team sports.
In Kabaddi, the raider's single-breath chant is called 'cant', and putting the whole opposing team out scores a 2-point Lona.
In Kho-Kho, 9 players take the field; chasers sit facing opposite directions and cannot cut across sitters.
Judo means 'gentle way'—it uses balance and leverage rather than brute force.
Wrestling is contested on a 9 m circular mat, with 3 officials awarding points by majority vote.
Freestyle wrestling allows using legs; Greco-Roman forbids holds below the waist.

problem.en: In Kabaddi, a raider crosses the bonus line before touching any defender, and then gets caught by the defenders. Does the raider get the bonus point?

why.en: A raider must cross the bonus line BEFORE touching or being caught by antis.

text.en: Since the raider crossed the bonus line cleanly before being caught, 1 bonus point is awarded (though the raider is out, giving 1 point to the defending team).

why.en: Bonus points are awarded when the bonus line is crossed prior to a touch or struggle.

prompt.en: Explain the meanings of 'cant' and 'Lona' in Kabaddi, and the difference between Freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling.

requiredIdeas.en: Cant is holding breath and chanting kabaddi in one expiration; Lona is a 2-point bonus for putting all opponents out
Freestyle wrestling allows leg holds and trips; Greco-Roman forbids attacking below the waist
Kho-Kho has 9 players on field per team with 9-minute turns

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Greco-Roman wrestling allows tripping with the legs

points.en: Kabaddi (13×10 m men, 12×8 m women) features cant, bonus line, and 2-point Lona.
Kho-Kho (9 of 12 players on field) has two innings of 9-minute chasing/running turns.
Judo ('gentle way') uses balance and leverage with 1 referee and 2 judges.
Wrestling (9 m circular mat) includes Freestyle (arms & legs) and Greco-Roman (above waist only).
